messages:
Jordan (support): Heads-up: customer ACME is seeing p95/p99 spikes on their Dedicated pool since 02:10 UTC. They report timeouts and a bunch of 503s. They called support.
Jordan (support): Quick summary from their logs: sudden traffic jump ~+3.5x at 02:08, then a bunch of queued requests. They say response times spiked to 12s p95 and 28s p99.
Arjun (oncall): Thanks — can you paste the pool id and the exact timestamps? Do we have metrics?
Jordan (support): Pool id: dedicated-prod-42. Spike window: 02:08:15 — 02:18:00 UTC. I uploaded the customer request ids to the ticket.
autoscale-bot: Autoscale event: pool=dedicated-prod-42 action=scale_up requested=4 actual=1 reason=burst_traffic timestamp=1778456495
Maria (sre): I’m seeing the same in infra metrics — the control-plane requested new nodes but node launch time shows a 5–7m cold-start. Looks like the cloud GPU nodes are slow to come up during that window.
Amy (infra): Confirmed. GCP preemptible T4s in us-west2 had a provisioning blip. Node provision latency median ~180s, tail ~420s for that hour.
Kevin (runtime): Runtime logs show lots of grpc deadlines on the serving frontends while waiting for backends to register. Also noticed autowarm jobs didn’t run because min_replicas was 0.
Jordan (support): Customer mentions they were on Dedicated with min_capacity=0 (cost-optimized). They expected autoscale to heal but it was too slow.
Lia (cs): Customer is pretty upset. Asking for mitigation and a postmortem. They want a temporary credit and guarantee no recurrence.
Arjun (oncall): Short-term mitigation ideas: 1) route traffic to hosted fallback (if allowed), 2) bump pool min_replicas temporarily, 3) pre-warm new nodes via a warmup job. Which is easiest right now?
Amy (infra): Quickest: bump min_replicas to 3 for that pool. I can do it in 2–3 mins. But we need to notify billing/CS.
Kevin (runtime): Also enable "prewarm=true" on the pool config so the scheduler pulls warm images and preloads KV caches as nodes come up. That reduces per-node warmup from ~80s to ~20s for model loading.
Maria (sre): Repro steps I used:
```
# list replicas
rictl get pool dedicated-prod-42 --output wide
# check node launches
gcloud compute instances list --filter="labels=ri-pool:dedicated-prod-42" --zone=us-west2*
# logs for autoscaler
kubectl -n ri-system logs deployment/ri-autoscaler --since=30m | grep dedicated-prod-42
```
Maria (sre): Observed autoscaler requested 4 but cloud returned only 1 within the SLO. Cloud API error 503 showed up intermittently.
Jordan (support): Customer-side repro: they replayed a traffic burst against their pool with the same concurrency and reproduced >p99 25s when min_replicas=0.
Arjun (oncall): Actions taken: Amy bumped min_replicas to 3 at 02:22 UTC -> nodes fully registered by 02:27 UTC -> p95 stabilized ~450ms, p99 ~900ms. Customer notified and confirmed better SLOs.
Amy (infra): Screenshot of scaling change (attached to ticket). Also I submitted a ticket to cloud provider about provisioning tail latency.
Kevin (runtime): Follow-ups: we should add a safety policy to prevent Dedicated pools used in production from having min_replicas=0. Suggestion: policy that warns in Console and a configurable org-level guard.
Lia (cs): Customer asked for a one-time credit. I’ve looped in finance. Also scheduled a postmortem call Wednesday.
Maria (sre): Longer-term mitigations:
- enforce min_replicas>=1 for prod-tagged pools by default
- implement a prewarm lifecycle hook that runs an init job to load the hot model weights and populate KV cache immediately after instance registration
- expose a "fast-failover" route to hosted pool when Dedicated capacity is degraded (opt-in)
- improve autoscaler backoff to retry faster if cloud errors are transient
Kevin (runtime): I’ll prototype a prewarm init container that runs `python warm_cache.py --model redwood-3b` and calls the runtime health endpoint. Should cut model load from ~40s to ~8–12s.
Arjun (oncall): For the postmortem, assign owners: infra -> Amy, runtime -> Kevin, sre -> Maria, support -> Jordan, cs -> Lia. Add timeline, root cause (cloud provisioning tail + min_replicas=0 config), and mitigations.
Jordan (support): Customer already accepted temporary credit offer and wants weekly updates until fixes in place.
Amy (infra): Filed infra ticket RI-9876 referencing provider incident and requested expedited capacity warm pool rollout.
Kevin (runtime): One more quick workaround we used earlier: for critical customers we can create a small warm pool (preprovisioned) in a cheaper region and route burst traffic there; requires config and networking checks.
Maria (sre): Note: we should also add alerting on queue length + average node registration time > 90s to catch this before p99 spikes.
Lia (cs): Noted. I’ll keep customer updated and will join postmortem.
Arjun (oncall): OK, closing the immediate incident. Please update the ticket with the actions and owners. 
Jordan (support): Thanks team — please paste any runbooks or config snippets here for the postmortem. :thumbsup:
Kevin (runtime): Paste of the quick warmup snippet we tested:
```
# warm_cache.py (toy)
import requests
m='redwood-3b'
requests.post('http://localhost:8080/internal/warm', json={'model': m, 'batch': 8})
```
Kevin (runtime): I also pushed a small PR to add a `prewarm` flag to pool config schema, draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/512
Maria (sre): I’ll draft the incident timeline and start the postmortem doc.
Amy (infra): Will follow up on provider side and post any updates.
Jordan (support): Closing thread here — ticket updated. Customer will expect a postmortem and the fixes listed.
